failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Answers added supplied role, institution, title, or place words, or used a different inflected form than the expected concise answer.

rejected_edits.content: - When a clue asks for the term for a described event or phenomenon, give the generic term at that level, not the full name of the particular instance found in context. Include the specific proper name only when the clue asks for the named event or entity.
rejected_edits.target: Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, in the conventional lexical form and part of speech called for by the clue (for example, an adjective or demonym rather than its associated country).

rejected_edits.content: - When a clue asks what a name, initialism, or abbreviation “stands for,” give its established expansion. Do not let a nearby idiom or dictionary definition override that explicit cue; resolve the whole clue before choosing which sense is requested.
rejected_edits.target: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use any proper-name cue to identify the requested name or name part.
